newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse pursues downward trend.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse pursues downward trend.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse closed its two-hour session on Tuesday 0.08 percent lower, pursuing its gradual decline which started in early November, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 431.95 points from 432.28 points on Monday.

"The drop in blue-chip Societe Nationale d'Investissment (SNI) has dramatically pulled down the bourse index...This confirms the downward trend of the bourse on profit taking," a market analyst at Upline Securities said.
SNI, which has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies, lost five dirhams to close at 535 dirhams.
SNI is Morocco's second largest private conglomerate with a market capitalisation of more than 5.5 billion dirhams.
ONA Group, the country's largest private group, remained stable at 475 dirhams, a broker said.
On the previous session, ONA was traded below the 500-dirham line for the first time since October. he added.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie lost one dirham to close at 315 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the liquid stocks, was unchanged at 395 dirhams.
Tuesday's traded volume was not immediately available.
